headline: KEPCO Confirms Large Data Breach Affecting 1.52 Million Customers
seoTitle: KEPCO Reports Data Breach Affecting 1.52 Million Users
metaDescription: The Korea Electric Power Corporation disclosed a significant data leak impacting over 1.5 million customers, following a smaller breach last month.
aiSummaryBullets: State-run utility provider KEPCO identified a data security breach impacting approximately 1.52 million individuals.
The compromised data includes users from the company's electronic procurement system and the KEPCO ON customer service platform.
This incident marks the second major data security disclosure from the organization within a one-month timeframe.
aiContextParagraph: The Korea Electric Power Corporation, known as KEPCO, is the primary state-run provider of electricity in South Korea. The utility company recently reported that it had been the target of a significant cyber incident resulting in the exposure of personal information belonging to 1.52 million users. According to the organization, the breach impacted 650,487 users registered on the KEPCO ON customer service platform and 869,761 participants associated with its electronic procurement system. This discovery follows a separate incident reported by the firm just one month prior, which involved a data leak affecting tens of thousands of people. The recurring nature of these security issues has prompted increased scrutiny regarding the management of consumer data within the state-run power utility. Investigations into the extent and nature of these unauthorized access events are ongoing as the company addresses the recent findings.
whyItIsViral: The event is trending due to reports from two independent national media outlets highlighting a significant and recurring failure in data security at a state-run utility.
